findings.reason: a worker told the move "was withheld" will look for a hold that never took the row, and the row that must be intercepted takes the observer branch with `held = None` set locally while `self._held[run_id]` persists.
findings.text: §29's Why states "the exception that prints a recovery needs the run to have been told, which happens only when a held row is released. So the move was withheld", but `_hold_settle` sets `self._told[run_id] = True` at the moment the stop is held (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1429`), not on release, so `_observer_exception` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1403-1409`, `told and to_state not in SETTLED_STATES`) fires when `stopped → working` arrives and that row is delivered (drawn blank, because its destination word equals the shown word), while the stop stays in `self._held` and is released by `_release_expired` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1380-1386`) at the window close — the fix belongs on the observer/held branch that runs at :1515-1519, not in a supersede-by-release path
